review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

2:1.sourceText: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἦλθον οὐ καθ’ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:1.targetText: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.

groups.note: κἀγώ ("and I") is the subject of the whole sentence; BSB repeats I in each clause and has no word for and.
ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ("superiority of speech") is rendered eloquence.
The genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ ("of God") is rendered about God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:2.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον.
2:2.targetText: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.

groups.note: οὐ … τι ("not … anything") is rendered nothing.
The demonstrative τοῦτον ("this one") is rendered Him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a temporal frame; the Greek has only ἐν ὑμῖν ("among you").

2:3.sourceText: κἀγὼ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ πολλῷ ἐγενόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
2:3.targetText: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.

groups.note: κἀγώ ("and I") is rendered I; BSB has no word for and here.
ἐγενόμην ("I was") with πρὸς ὑμᾶς is rendered came to you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat in before fear.

2:4.sourceText: καὶ ὁ λόγος μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμά μου οὐκ ἐν πειθοῖς σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀποδείξει Πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως,
2:4.targetText: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for this καί ("and" or "both") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins Spirit and power as the Spirit’s power, so καί ("and") has no counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

2:5.sourceText: ἵνα ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν μὴ ᾖ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ.
2:5.targetText: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.

groups.note: ᾖ ("be") is rendered would rest.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:6.sourceText: Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις, σοφίαν δὲ οὐ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐδὲ τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τῶν καταργουμένων·
2:6.targetText: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

groups.note: The article with the participle, τῶν καταργουμένων ("the ones being brought to nothing"), is rendered who are coming to nothing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a message of; the Greek object is σοφίαν ("wisdom") itself.

2:7.sourceText: ἀλλὰ λαλοῦμεν Θεοῦ σοφίαν ἐν μυστηρίῳ, τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην, ἣν προώρισεν ὁ Θεὸς πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς δόξαν ἡμῶν·
2:7.targetText: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.

groups.note: ἀλλά ("but, rather") is rendered No.
ἐν μυστηρίῳ ("in a mystery") is rendered mysterious.
The article with the participle, τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην ("the one that has been hidden"), is rendered the … hidden.
ὁ Θεός ("God") is rendered He.
αἰώνων ("the ages") is rendered time began.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two descriptions of wisdom with and.

2:8.sourceText: ἣν οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἔγνωκεν· εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν Κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν·
2:8.targetText: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

groups.note: ἔγνωσαν ("they had known") is rendered they had, with understood implied.
ἄν with the aorist marks the unreal result, would have.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:9.sourceText: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται Ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη, ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
2:9.targetText: Rather, as it is written:  “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”

groups.note: The relative Ἅ ("the things that") and ὅσα ("all that") refer to the same things; BSB renders them once as what.
ἐπὶ … ἀνέβη ("has come up into" the heart) is rendered has imagined.
The article with the participle, τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν ("for the ones loving"), is rendered for those who love.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the clauses without and.
BSB lists the clauses without and.
BSB has no word for ἀνθρώπου ("of man") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:10.sourceText: ἡμῖν γὰρ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος· τὸ γὰρ Πνεῦμα πάντα ἐραυνᾷ, καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:10.targetText: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit.  The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered But.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated.

2:11.sourceText: τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ; οὕτως καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ἔγνωκεν εἰ μὴ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:11.targetText: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

groups.note: The article τά is used as a pronoun ("the things"), rendered the thoughts.
τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ("of the man") is rendered his own.

2:12.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν·
2:12.targetText: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

groups.note: The article τό is used as a relative ("who").
τὰ … χαρισθέντα ("the things freely given") is rendered actively, what … has freely given.

2:13.sourceText: ἃ καὶ λαλοῦμεν οὐκ ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλ’ ἐν διδακτοῖς Πνεύματος, πνευματικοῖς πνευματικὰ συνκρίνοντες.
2:13.targetText: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.

groups.note: The relative ἅ ("which things") is rendered what.
καί ("also") is rendered And.
λόγοις is understood again in the second clause.
The dative adjective πνευματικοῖς ("with spiritual things") is rendered in spiritual words.
The neuter adjective πνευματικά ("spiritual things") is rendered spiritual truths.
συνκρίνοντες ("combining, interpreting") is rendered expressing.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies this is to open the sentence.

2:14.sourceText: ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Θεοῦ· μωρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστίν, καὶ οὐ δύναται γνῶναι, ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται.
2:14.targetText: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

groups.note: The article τά is used as a pronoun ("the things").
The genitive τοῦ Πνεύματος ("of the Spirit") is rendered from the Spirit.
The singular ἐστίν ("it is") is rendered they are, referring to the things.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative frame for the genitive.

2:15.sourceText: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει μὲν πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ’ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται.
2:15.targetText: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.

groups.note: ὑπ’ οὐδενός ("by no one") is rendered not … anyone’s.
The passive ἀνακρίνεται ("is judged") is rendered is … subject to … judgment.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for δέ here.
BSB’s Greek text differs here; μέν ("on the one hand") has no English counterpart.

2:16.sourceText: τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου, ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν; ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν Χριστοῦ ἔχομεν.
2:16.targetText: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

groups.note: The relative ὅς with the future ("who will") expresses result, rendered so as.
